---
title: "Module 1: Types of survey questions"
---

Every variable in your research has a **level of measurement**. The question type you choose decides what kind of data you get and which statistics you can run later.

## Variables and question types

In research, a **variable** is any characteristic you measure or record for each participant, such as age, sex, or weight. Variables are divided into two main types:

**Numerical variables** are measured as numbers, and calculations such as mean or median.

- *Discrete*: whole numbers that are counted, such as age in years or number of children.
- *Continuous*: measurements that can have decimals, such as blood sugar, height, haemoglobin, and most other biomarker values.

**Categorical variables** place each participant into a group or category.

- *Nominal*: categories with no natural order, such as sex, blood group, or hair color.
- *Ordinal*: categories with a meaningful order, such as education level, pain severity, cancer stage, or a Likert scale.

Dates, times and free-text answers are also collected in surveys. **The table below shows which question type to use in KoboToolbox for each type of variable**.

| Variable type | Description | Examples | Question type in KoboToolbox |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **Numerical, discrete** | Whole numbers (counts) | Age in years, number of children | `integer` |
| **Numerical, continuous** | Measurements with decimals | Blood sugar, height, haemoglobin | `decimal` |
| **Categorical, nominal** | Categories with no order | Sex, blood group, type of cancer | `select_one` / `select_multiple` |
| **Categorical, ordinal** | Categories with a meaningful order | Education level, cancer stage, Likert scale | `select_one` |
| **Date and time** | Calendar dates or clock times | Date of admission, time of birth | `date` / `time` / `datetime` |
| **Text** | Free, open-ended answers | "Other, specify", comments | `text` |
| **None (information only)** | Shows a message; no answer is collected | Introduction, section instructions, thank-you message | `note` |

## Common question types in XLSForm (KoboToolbox)

In an XLSForm, each question has a **question type**, written in the `type` column of the `survey` sheet. These are the question types most often used in research questionnaires:

| Question type | What it collects | Example |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `integer` | Whole number | Age in completed years |
| `decimal` | Number with decimals | Weight (kg) |
| `range` | Number chosen on a slider or scale | Pain score 0–10 |
| `text` | Free text | Other occupation |
| `select_one list_name` | One option from a list | Marital status |
| `select_multiple list_name` | One or more options from a list | Symptoms experienced |
| `date` | Date | Date of admission |
| `time` | Time | Time of medication |
| `datetime` | Date and time | Date and time of delivery |
| `note` | Displays information, no answer collected | Section instructions |
| `acknowledge` | A single "OK" confirmation | Consent statement read |
| `geopoint` | GPS location | Household location |
| `image` | Photo | Photo of a wound or document |
| `audio` | Audio recording | Recorded interview |
| `barcode` | Scans a barcode or QR code | Patient ID card |
| `calculate` | Hidden calculation, not shown to respondent | Total knowledge score |
| `begin_group` / `end_group` | Groups questions into sections | Section A: Demographics |

The rest of this module looks closely at the seven question types you will use most: integer, decimal, single option, multiple option, date and time, text, and note.

::: {.callout-tip}
## More question types and advanced features
XLSForm supports many more question types and options, such as repeat groups, file uploads, and cascading selects. For the full list with examples, visit the [XLSForm question types reference](https://xlsform.org/en/#question-types).
:::

## Integer (whole number)

Used for counts and ages in completed years. No decimal point is allowed.

> **Poll:** How many years have you worked as a nurse?

- Examples: age in years, number of children, parity, number of hospital admissions, days of hospital stay.
- Analysis: mean, median, SD, t-test, correlation.

## Decimal

Used for measurements that need a fractional part.

> **Poll:** What is your height in metres? (e.g. 1.62)

- Examples: weight (kg), height (m), haemoglobin (g/dL), body temperature (°C), BMI.
- Tip: always write the **unit** in the question.

## Single option (select one)

The respondent can choose **only one** answer from a list.

> **Poll:** In which inpatient department do you currently work? ☐ Medical ☐ Surgical ☐ Paediatric ☐ Maternity ☐ Critical care

- Examples: sex, marital status, education level, yes/no questions.
- Categories must not overlap, and must cover every possible answer (add "Other" if needed).

## Multiple option (select multiple)

The respondent can choose **one or more** answers.

> **Poll:** Which sources do you use to learn about research methods? (select all that apply) ☐ Textbooks ☐ Journals ☐ YouTube ☐ Teachers ☐ AI tools

- Examples: symptoms experienced, sources of health information, comorbidities.
- In the data, each option becomes its own yes/no.

## Date and time

> **Poll:** On what date did you join the M.Sc. Nursing programme?  
> **Poll:** At what time does your morning duty usually start?

- `date`: date of admission, date of delivery, last menstrual period.
- `time`: time of medication, time of birth.
- `datetime`: exact date **and** time of an event.
- Digital forms use a date picker, so there are no confusing formats like 05/06/2026.

## Text

Free, open-ended answers.

> **Poll:** In one word, what is the biggest challenge in collecting thesis data?

- Examples: "Other (please specify)", suggestions, comments, qualitative answers.
- Use text questions only when needed. They take longer to answer and are harder to analyse.

## Note

A note shows information to the respondent or data collector but **collects no answer**.

> Example: *"This survey has 25 questions and takes about 10 minutes to complete. Your answers will be kept confidential."*

- Use notes for introductions, section instructions, and thank-you messages.


## Quiz: choose the question type

For each question, click the XLSForm question type you would use. Then press **Check answers**.

```{=html}
<div id="qt-quiz"></div>

<style>
  #qt-quiz fieldset {
    border: 1px solid #dee2e6;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--course-color, #2780e3);
    border-radius: 6px;
    padding: 0.8rem 1rem;
    margin-bottom: 1rem;
  }
  #qt-quiz legend {
    font-size: 1rem;
    font-weight: 600;
    float: none;
    width: auto;
    padding: 0 0.3rem;
    margin-bottom: 0.3rem;
  }
  #qt-quiz label {
    display: block;
    padding: 0.25rem 0.4rem;
    border-radius: 4px;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  #qt-quiz label:hover { background: #f1f6fd; }
  #qt-quiz input { margin-right: 0.5rem; }
  #qt-quiz code { font-size: 0.95rem; }
  #qt-quiz .qt-right { background: #e6f4ea; border-left-color: #1e7b4f; }
  #qt-quiz .qt-wrong { background: #fdecea; border-left-color: #c0392b; }
  #qt-quiz .qt-feedback { margin-top: 0.4rem; font-size: 0.95rem; }
  #qt-quiz .qt-buttons button {
    background: var(--course-color, #2780e3);
    color: #fff;
    border: none;
    border-radius: 5px;
    padding: 0.5rem 1.2rem;
    margin-right: 0.5rem;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  #qt-quiz .qt-score {
    font-size: 1.15rem;
    font-weight: 700;
    margin: 1rem 0;
    color: var(--course-color, #2780e3);
  }
</style>

<script>
(function () {
  const questions = [
    { q: "How many times have you been admitted to hospital in the past year?",
      options: ["integer", "decimal", "text", "select_one"], answer: 0,
      why: "It is a count, so a whole number." },
    { q: "What is your haemoglobin level (g/dL)?",
      options: ["integer", "decimal", "text", "note"], answer: 1,
      why: "It is a measurement that needs decimals." },
    { q: "What is your marital status?",
      options: ["select_multiple", "text", "select_one", "integer"], answer: 2,
      why: "Only one status applies to each person." },
    { q: "Which symptoms have you had in the last 7 days? (select all that apply)",
      options: ["select_one", "select_multiple", "text", "note"], answer: 1,
      why: "More than one symptom can be chosen." },
    { q: "On what date were you admitted to this hospital?",
      options: ["time", "datetime", "date", "text"], answer: 2,
      why: "Only a calendar date is needed." },
    { q: "At what time do you usually take your medicine?",
      options: ["date", "time", "integer", "datetime"], answer: 1,
      why: "Only a clock time is needed." },
    { q: "What was the exact date and time of delivery?",
      options: ["date", "time", "datetime", "text"], answer: 2,
      why: "Both the date and the time are needed." },
    { q: "If your occupation is \"Other\", please specify.",
      options: ["select_one", "note", "text", "select_multiple"], answer: 2,
      why: "It is a free, open-ended answer." },
    { q: "\"Section B: The next questions are about your daily activities. Please       answer honestly.\"",
      options: ["text", "note", "select_one", "integer"], answer: 1,
      why: "It only shows instructions; no answer is collected." },
    { q: "How satisfied are you with nursing care? (Very dissatisfied to Very satisfied)",
      options: ["select_multiple", "integer", "text", "select_one"], answer: 3,
      why: "It is an ordered scale (Likert) where one option is chosen." }
  ];

  const box = document.getElementById("qt-quiz");

  function render() {
    let html = "";
    questions.forEach((item, i) => {
      html += `<fieldset id="qt-q${i}"><legend>${i + 1}. ${item.q}</legend>`;
      item.options.forEach((opt, j) => {
        html += `<label><input type="radio" name="qt${i}" value="${j}"><code>${opt}</code></label>`;
      });
      html += `<div class="qt-feedback"></div></fieldset>`;
    });
    html += `<div class="qt-score"></div>
             <div class="qt-buttons">
               <button type="button" id="qt-check">Check answers</button>
               <button type="button" id="qt-reset" style="display:none">Try again</button>
             </div>`;
    box.innerHTML = html;
    document.getElementById("qt-check").onclick = check;
    document.getElementById("qt-reset").onclick = render;
  }

  function check() {
    let score = 0;
    questions.forEach((item, i) => {
      const fs = document.getElementById(`qt-q${i}`);
      const chosen = fs.querySelector("input:checked");
      const feedback = fs.querySelector(".qt-feedback");
      const correct = `<code>${item.options[item.answer]}</code>`;
      fs.querySelectorAll("input").forEach(inp => inp.disabled = true);

      if (chosen && Number(chosen.value) === item.answer) {
        score++;
        fs.classList.add("qt-right");
        feedback.innerHTML = `✅ Correct: ${correct}. ${item.why}`;
      } else {
        fs.classList.add("qt-wrong");
        const yours = chosen ? "" : "Not answered. ";
        feedback.innerHTML = `❌ ${yours}Correct answer: ${correct}. ${item.why}`;
      }
    });
    box.querySelector(".qt-score").textContent =
      `Your score: ${score} out of ${questions.length}`;
    document.getElementById("qt-check").style.display = "none";
    document.getElementById("qt-reset").style.display = "inline-block";
  }

  render();
})();
</script>
```
::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answers (click to show)

| No. | Answer | Why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `integer` | A count, so a whole number |
| 2 | `decimal` | A measurement with decimals |
| 3 | `select_one` | Only one status applies |
| 4 | `select_multiple` | More than one symptom can be chosen |
| 5 | `date` | A calendar date |
| 6 | `time` | A clock time |
| 7 | `datetime` | Both date and time are needed |
| 8 | `text` | A free, open-ended answer |
| 9 | `note` | Information only; no answer is collected |
| 10 | `select_one` | An ordered scale where one option is chosen (Likert) |
:::
